meaning_long: claiming to love something you are actually afraid of
source: 《新序·杂事》 (public domain), retold in our own words.
cover: He LOVED dragons…\Nuntil he met one.
hook: He LOVED dragons…\Nuntil he met one.
meaning: = loving the idea, not the real thing
story: Ancient China. Lord Ye loves dragons more than anything: dragons carved on his pillars, painted on his walls, embroidered on his clothes, even on his cups. He tells everyone how much he loves dragons. A real dragon in the sky hears about this, is very touched, and flies down to visit him. It happily pokes its head through Lord Ye's window to say hello. Lord Ye screams in terror and runs away. He never loved real dragons, only the idea of them.
continuity: - LORD YE: chubby noble about 40, round face, thin curled mustache, tall black hat, rich green robe embroidered with little dragon patterns (pictures only, no characters).
- THE DRAGON: a long, friendly Chinese dragon with jade-green scales, a golden mane and whiskers, big round curious eyes and a gentle, happy, shy smile. Never scary, never angry, no fire.
- LORD YE'S HOUSE: a grand wooden hall with red pillars carved with dragons, dragon paintings on the walls, a round wooden lattice window, a courtyard outside.
- SETTING: ancient China, soft daylight; the sky with soft grey ink-wash clouds.
scenes: The twist (used as the hook, first frame of the video)

Inside Lord Ye's hall full of carved and painted dragons: the friendly real dragon pokes its big head through the round window with a happy, hopeful smile. Lord Ye leaps backwards in terror, hat flying off, mouth wide open screaming, arms flailing. Both faces clear. This is the most important image; the editor will push in on it.
Lord Ye stands in his hall hugging a small carved wooden dragon statue, eyes closed in bliss, surrounded by dragon carvings on the pillars. (Only Lord Ye.)

Wide shot of Lord Ye's hall: dragons carved on every pillar, painted on the walls and screens, dragon patterns on his robe; Lord Ye sips from a cup with a dragon painted on it, very pleased. (Only Lord Ye.)
Lord Ye stands in his courtyard with arms spread wide, shouting happily to the sky, chest puffed out, clearly boasting. (Only Lord Ye.)
Up in the clouds, the friendly jade-green dragon hears him, its eyes sparkling, a big touched smile, a tiny happy tear. It starts to fly down. (Only the dragon.)
Outside the house: the dragon curls its long body around the roof and gently pokes its head toward the round lattice window, shy and excited, like a fan meeting its hero. (Only the dragon.)
Lord Ye runs out of the back of his hall in total panic, robe flying, one shoe falling off, hat gone, arms in the air. Behind him through the doorway the dragon looks confused and sad.
The window (background for the big title)

The round wooden lattice window from inside, now empty, with a single golden dragon whisker lying on the windowsill in the lower half of the frame. The upper half is a calm, plain wall with soft grey ink washes and almost nothing on it (we place the big title there). No people, no dragon.

A modern apartment: the same LORD YE (round face, curled mustache) in a green hoodie printed with simple tree pictures (no text), standing among nature posters (pictures only, no text), leaps onto a chair screaming at one tiny spider on the floor. No other people. No text, no logos.
lines: He loved dragons more than anything, until he met one.
Lord Ye was crazy about dragons.
Dragons on his walls, his cups, his clothes.
He told everyone: I love dragons!
A real dragon heard, and came to visit.
It poked its head through his window.
Lord Ye screamed and ran away!
It means you only love the idea of something.
Like loving nature… until you see a spider.
title: He loved dragons… until a real one came to visit 🐉 | 叶公好龙
desc: 叶公好龙 (yè gōng hào lóng) = loving the idea of something, not the real thing. Ever done that? 👇
pinned: 叶 Ye · 公 lord · 好 love · 龙 dragon. 📝 他说喜欢运动，可一叫他跑步就躲，真是叶公好龙。(Tā shuō xǐhuan yùndòng, kě yí jiào tā pǎobù jiù duǒ, zhēn shì yè gōng hào lóng.) = He says he loves sports, but hides whenever you ask him to go running. That's Lord Ye loving dragons.
